definition: A medical device that is a recording. Physical type definition: a storage device on which information (sounds or images) have been recorded
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical compact disk
definition: A medical device that is a compact disk. Physical type definition: a digitally encoded recording on an optical disk that is smaller than a phonograph record; played back by a laser
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical CD-R
definition: A medical device that is a CD-R. Physical type definition: a compact disc on which you can write only once and thereafter is read-only memory
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical lamp
definition: A medical device that is a lamp. Physical type definition: an artificial source of visible illumination
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical fluorescent lamp
definition: A medical device that is a fluorescent lamp. Physical type definition: lamp consisting of a tube coated on the inside with a fluorescent material; mercury vapor in the tube emits ultraviolet radiation that is converted to visible radiation by the fluorescent material
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical sodium-vapor lamp
definition: A medical device that is a sodium-vapor lamp. Physical type definition: lamp in which an electric current passed through a tube of sodium vapor makes a yellow light; used is street lighting
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical display
definition: A medical device that is a display. Physical type definition: an electronic device that represents information in visual form
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical flat panel display
definition: A medical device that is a flat panel display. Physical type definition: a type of video display that is thin and flat; commonly used in laptop computers
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: medical electromechanical device
definition: A medical device that is a electromechanical device. Physical type definition: a mechanical device that is operated by electricity
source: FDA physical-head scope and WordNet native inclusion

label: internal-combustion-powered car
definition: A car configuration powered by an internal combustion engine.

label: gasoline-powered car
definition: A car configuration whose documented powertrain is gasoline.

label: diesel-powered car
definition: A car configuration whose documented powertrain is diesel.

label: electric-powered car
definition: A car configuration whose documented powertrain is electric.

label: hybrid-powered car
definition: A car configuration whose documented powertrain is hybrid.

label: mid-ocean ridge
definition: "An underwater mountain range, formed by plate tectonics. This uplifting of the ocean floor occurs when convection currents rise in the mantle beneath the oceanic crust and create magma where two tectonic plates meet at a divergent boundary. The mid-ocean ridges of the world are connected and form a single global mid-oceanic ridge system that is part of every ocean." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-ocean_ridge]

label: range of seamounts
definition: "A mountain range which is submerged under a marine water body." []

label: seamount
definition: "A mountain rising from the ocean seafloor that does not reach to the water's surface (sea level), and thus is not an island. Typically formed from volcanoes that rise abruptly and are usually found rising from a seafloor of 1,000 - 4,000 meters depth. Independent features that rise to at least 1,000 meters above the seafloor." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seamount]

label: guyot
definition: "A flat-topped seamount." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyot]

label: terrestrial mountain
definition: "A mountain which is located on land and which is bounded by an atmosphere or outer space." []

label: polar mountain
definition: "A mountain that is part of a polar environment." [https://www.unep-wcmc.org/resources-and-data/mountain-watch--environmental-change-sustainable-development-in-mountains]

label: temperate mountain
definition: "A mountain that is part of a temperate environment." [https://www.unep-wcmc.org/resources-and-data/mountain-watch--environmental-change-sustainable-development-in-mountains]

label: tropical mountain
definition: "A mountain that is part of a tropical environment." [https://www.unep-wcmc.org/resources-and-data/mountain-watch--environmental-change-sustainable-development-in-mountains]

label: high-elevation mountain
definition: "A mountain which has a maximum elevation greater than 2500 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, http://www.wikialps.eu/doku.php?id=wiki\:mountain_and_mountain_area, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: mid-elevation mountain
definition: "A mountain which has a maximum elevation between 300 and 2499 metres above sea level and slopes greater than or equal to two degrees of inclination." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, http://www.wikialps.eu/doku.php?id=wiki\:mountain_and_mountain_area, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 1 mountain
definition: "A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation greater than 4500 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 2 mountain
definition: "A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 3500 and 4500 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 3 mountain
definition: "A high-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 2500 and 3500 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 4 mountain
definition: "A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 1500 and 2499 metres above sea level and a slope greater than or equal to two degrees." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 5 mountain
definition: "A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 1000 and 1499 metres above sea level and either 1) a slope greater than or equal to five degrees or 2) a local elevation range, within a 7 kilometre radius, of greater than 300 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: UNEP-WCMC class 6 mountain
definition: "A mid-elevation mountain which has a maximum elevation between 300 and 999 metres above sea level and a local elevation range, within a 7 kilometre radius, of greater than 300 metres above sea level." [http://dx.doi.org/10.1079/9780851994468.0004, https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20080511044709/http\://www.unep-wcmc.org/mountains/mountain_watch/pdfs/WholeReport.pdf, https://www.cabi.org/cabebooks/ebook/20000614040]

label: underground river
definition: "A river that is under the surface of the Earth." [MA:ma]

label: freshwater river
definition: "A river where fresh water flows." [ORCID:0000-0002-4366-3088]

label: geothermally heated river
definition: "A river which is heated by geothermal processes such as heat exchange with lava or hydrothermal percolation." [http://www.atlasobscura.com/places/the-boiling-river-of-the-amazon]

label: polluted river
definition: "A river which has elevated levels of contaminants." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollution, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_pollution]

label: saline lake
definition: "A lake whose water contains a considerable concentration of dissolved salts." [MA:ma]

label: freshwater lake
definition: "A lake of whose water contains low concentrations of salts." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater]

label: reservoir
definition: "An artificial body of water, often contained by a dam, constructed for the purpose of water storage." [MA:ma]

label: volcanic crater lake
definition: "A lake contained within a volcanic crater." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crater_lake, MA:ma]

label: underground lake
definition: "A lake which is formed under the surface of the Earth. Such a lake may be associated with caves and aquifers and springs." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: asphalt lake
definition: "A lake formed of a natural deposit of alphalt, a black, highly viscous liquid or semi-solid composed of fossil hydrocarbons." [MA:ma]

label: endorheic lake
definition: "A lake from which there is no outflow of water, either on the surface as rivers, or underground by flow or diffusion through rock or permeable material." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endorheic]

label: ice-covered lake
definition: "A lake permanently covered by ice." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: meromictic lake
definition: "A lake which has layers of water which do not intermix." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: periglacial lake
definition: "A lake, part of whose margin is formed by an ice mass, ice cap or glacier, the ice having obstructed the natural drainage of the land." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: fjord lake
definition: "A lake in a glacially eroded valley, which has been eroded below sea level." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: oxbow lake
definition: "A lake which is formed when a wide meander from a stream or a river is cut off to form a lake. They are called oxbow lakes due to the distinctive curved shape that results from this process." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes]

label: rift lake
definition: "A lake which fills a depression that has formed as a result of subsidence along a a rift zone, an area of extensional tectonics in the continental crust." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Types_of_lakes] {comment="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_lake"}

label: artificial lake
definition: "A lake purposefully constructed." [MA:ma]

label: canal head reservoir
definition: "A reservoir constructed for the purpose of maintaining water levels in a canal or canals." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservoir]

label: proglacial lake
definition: "A lake formed either by the damming action of a moraine or ice dam during the retreat of a melting glacier, or one formed by meltwater trapped against an ice mass due to isostatic depression of the crust around the ice." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proglacial_lake]

label: flood control reservoir
definition: "A reservoir constructed for the purpose of containing a flood, an overflow of water from a body of water that sumerges land." [MA:ma]

label: hydroelectric reservoir
definition: "A reservoir constructed for the purpose of generating electricity." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservoir]

label: drinking water reservoir
definition: "A reservoir constructed for the purpose of providing drinking water." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservoir]

label: irrigation reservoir
definition: "A reservoir constructed for the purpose of providing water for irrigation." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservoir]

label: amenity lake
definition: "A lake constructed, or modified, for the chief purpose of providing an amenity." [MA:ma]

label: ribbon lake
definition: "A lake that is long, narrow, and finger-shaped, usually found in a glacial trough. Its formation begins when a glacier moves over an area containing alternate bands of hard and soft bedrock. The sharp-edged boulders carried at the bottom of the glacier erode the softer rock more quickly by abrasion, thus creating a hollow called a rock basin. On either side of the rock basin, the more resistant rock is eroded less and these outcrops of harder rock are known as rock bars, which act as dams between which rainwater may accumulate after the retreat of the ice age, filling up the rock basin and creating a ribbon lake. A ribbon lake may also form behind a terminal or recessional moraine, both of which also act as dams, enabling water to accumulate behind them. A ribbon lake may also occur if a tributary glacier joins a main glacier. The increase in power can create a trough, which is filled with water from a river/meltwater to create a ribbon lake." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribbon_lake]

label: tarn
definition: "A mountain lake that is formed in a cirque excavated by a glacier. A moraine may form a natural dam below a tarn." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarn_(lake)]

label: paternoster lake
definition: "One of a series of glacial lakes connected by a single stream or a braided stream system." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paternoster_lake]

label: glacial lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of glacial meltwater and which fills a depression formed as a result of a glacial erosion process." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacial_lake]

label: container of an intermittent oxbow lake
definition: "A depression which is continous with one or more abandoned meander loops of a river channel." [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4366-3088, https://www.britannica.com/science/oxbow-lake, MA:ma]

label: brackish lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of brackish water, having a higher salinity than fresh water but a lower salinity than marine water." []

label: alkaline salt lake
definition: "A saline lake which has a high pH." []

label: amictic lake
definition: "A lake which is permanently covered by ice, does not mix, and exhibit inverse cold water stratification whereby water temperature increases with depth below the ice surface." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amictic_lake]

label: holomictic lake
definition: "A holomictic lake is a lake which mixes at least once per year. Mixing is caused by a uniform temperature distribution from the upper to lower layers of the lake." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holomictic]

label: dimictic lake
definition: "A dimitic lake is a holomictic lake which mixes from top to bottom during two mixing periods each year. Mixing typically occurs during the spring and autumn, when the lake is \"isothermal\" (i.e., at the same temperature from the top to the bottom). At this time the water throughout the lake is about 4°C, and, in the absence of any temperature or density differences, the lake readily mixes from top to bottom. These lakes are common in regions with temperate climates." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimictic_lake]

label: polymictic lake
definition: "A polymictic lake is a holomictic lake which is too shallow to allow thermal stratification and which can mix from top to bottom through the ice-free period of the year." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymictic]

label: monomictic lake
definition: "A monomictic  lake is a holomictic lake which mixes from top to bottom during one mixing period each year." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monomictic]

label: cold monomictic lake
definition: "A monomictic lake which is covered by ice throughout much of the year and only mixes when its surface ice melts and the lake lacks thermal stratification." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monomictic]

label: warm monomictic lake
definition: "A monomictic lake which does not freeze and is thermally stratified throughout most of the year, only mixing in winter when cooler temperatures ease stratification." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monomictic]

label: cold polymictic lake
definition: "A cold polymictic lake is a polymictic lake which is covered by ice in winter." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymictic]

label: warm polymictic lake
definition: "A warm polymictic lake is a polymictic lake which is not covered by ice at any point during the year." [DOI:10.1139/f83-207, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymictic]

label: eutrophic lake
definition: "A lake which has nutrient-rich water." []

label: polluted lake
definition: "A lake which has concentrations of environmental contaminants high enough to harm the ecosystems associated with it." []

label: oligotrophic lake
definition: "A lake which has nutrient-poor water." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trophic_state_index]

label: mesotrophic lake
definition: "A lake with medium nutrient levels, which allow moderate productivity." []

label: exorheic lake
definition: "A lake from which water constantly flows out of under almost all climatic circumstances, maintaining low concentrations of dissolved solid relative to endorheic lakes." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_and_closed_lakes]

label: hypereutrophic lake
definition: "A lake which is composed primarily of water with very high nutrient concentrations." [https://github.com/EnvironmentOntology/envo/issues/529]

label: hypersaline lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of water with a concentration of dissolved salts greater than that of ocean water." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypersaline_lake]

label: humic lake
definition: "A lake which is composed primarily water with high concentrations of humic substances and organic acids, resulting in brown- or tea-coloured colouration." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dystrophic_lake]

label: natural lake
definition: "A lake which has formed as the result of processes that are not or are only minimally driven by human activity." []

label: caldera lake
definition: "A lake which is contained within a caldera." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crater_lake]

label: crater lake
definition: "A lake contained within a crater." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crater_lake, MA:ma]

label: meteorite lake
definition: "A lake which is contained in a crater formed by a meteorite impact." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Meteorite_.28extraterrestrial_impact.2F_crater.29_lakes]

label: impact crater lake
definition: "A lake which is contained in a crater formed by an impact event." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Meteorite_.28extraterrestrial_impact.2F_crater.29_lakes]

label: anoxic lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of anoxic water." []

label: lake with an anoxic hypolimnion
definition: "A lake which has a hypolimnion composed primarily of anoxic water." [http://dx.doi.org/10.4319/lo.1984.29.1.0111]

label: lake with a hypoxic hypolimnion
definition: "A lake which has a hypolimnion composed primarily of hypoxic water." [http://dx.doi.org/10.4319/lo.1984.29.1.0111]

label: hypoxic lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of hypoxic water." []

label: oxic lake
definition: "A lake which is primarily composed of oxic water." []

label: lake with an oxic hypolimnion
definition: "A lake which has a hypolimnion composed primarily of oxic water." [http://dx.doi.org/10.4319/lo.1984.29.1.0111]

label: tectonic lake
definition: "A lake which is contained in a depression formed by the deformation and resulting lateral and vertical movements of a lithosphere." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Tectonic_lakes]

label: aeolian lake
definition: "A lake which fills a basin that has been dammed by wind-blown sand,  formed between sand dunes oriented by winds; or formed by wind action under previously arid paleoenvironments." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Aeolian_lakes]

label: landslide lake
definition: "A lake which fills a depression where drainage is blocked by solid material transported by a landslide." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Landslide_lakes]

label: rockslide lake
definition: "A lake which fills a depression where drainage is blocked by solid material transported by a rockslide." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake#Landslide_lakes]

label: supraglacial lake
definition: "A water body which is located in a depression within the surface of a glacier." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supraglacial_lake]

label: intraglacial lake
definition: "A lake which is comprised of meltwater located underneath or within a glacier." [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258663667_Detection_of_a_subglacial_lake_in_Glacier_de_Tete_Rousse_Mont_Blanc_area_France, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313281555_Antarctic_subglacial_lakes_drain_through_sediment-floored_canals_Theory_and_model_testing_on_real_and_idealized_domains]

label: thermokarst lake
definition: "A freshwater lake which fills a depression formed by the erosion of thermokarst caused by permafrost thaw." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermokarst]

label: methane-releasing thermokarst lake
definition: "A thermokarst lake through which methane gas released from thawing permafrost, or other methane stores, rises and escapes to the atmosphere." [http://www.sciencealert.com/photos-reveal-more-than-200-bright-blue-arctic-lakes-have-started-bubbling-with-methane-gas]

label: subglacial lake
definition: "A lake which is situated beneath a glacier." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subglacial_lake]

label: marine lake
definition: "A lake which is connected to a marine water body via tunnels or cracks in the soil." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_lake]

label: artificial island
definition: "An island constructed by human effort." [MA:ma]

label: mangrove island
definition: "An island formed of trees and shrubs that grow in saline coastal habitats in the tropics and subtropics." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangrove]

label: atoll
definition: "An oceanic island, often having a characteristic ring-like shape surrounding a lagoon. Atolls are formed when coral reef grows around a volcanic island that later subsides into the ocean." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atoll]

label: continental island
definition: "An island that lies on a continental shelf." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island#Continental_island]

label: oceanic island
definition: "An island that does not sit on a continental shelf, and is of volcanic origin." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island#Oceanic_islands]

label: land-tied island
definition: "A continental island connected to its adjacent land by a natural feature, such as a causeway." [MA:ma]

label: ephemeral island
definition: "An island, usually the consequence of the activity of a submarine volcano, that only exists for a short period or short periods of time after its formation, then being eroded or otherwise disappearing beneath the surface of a body of water." [MA:ma]

label: river island
definition: "An island that lies in a river." [MA:ma]

label: lake island
definition: "An island that lies in a lake." [MA:ma]

label: skerry
definition: "An island which is small, principally composed of rock, and usually too small for human habitation." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skerry]

label: desert island
definition: "An island that is not permanently populated by humans." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_island]

label: cay
definition: "An island which is small, low in elevation, sandy, and located on the surface of a coral reef." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cay]

label: microcontinental island
definition: "An island created when a continent is rifted." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island]

label: depositional island
definition: "An island formed by deposition of solid material such as sand or small rocks where a water current loses some of its carrying capacity." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island]

label: barrier island
definition: "An island formed by the accumulation of sand deposited by sea currents on a continental shelves" [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island]

label: sea beach
definition: "A beach which is part of a sea shore." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach]

label: lacustrine beach
definition: "A beach which is part of a lake shore." [MA:ma]

label: raised beach
definition: "A beach or wave cut platform raised above the shore line by a relative fall in the sea level." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raised_beach]

label: machair
definition: "A fertile low-lying raised beach found on the some of the coastlines of Ireland and Scotland, in particular in the Outer Hebrides." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machair_%28geography%29]

label: shingle beach
definition: "A beach which is armoured with pebbles or small to medium sized cobbles." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shingle_beach]

label: sandy beach
definition: "A beach which is primarily composed of sand." []

label: wadi
definition: "A valley or ravine, bounded by relatively steep banks, which in the rainy season becomes a watercourse." [Geonames:feature]

label: dry valley
definition: "A valley which no longer has water flowing or accumulating over its surface." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_valley]

label: stream valley
definition: "A valley that contains, and has been formed by, a stream." [MA:ma]

label: cirque
definition: "A depression which is semicircular or crescent-shaped, found towards the crest of a mountain, and formed by the erosional processes caused by the motion of a glacier." [http://www.antarctica.ac.uk/apc/genericterms.html, http://www.thefreedictionary.com/Glacial+cirque, USGS:SDTS]

label: canyon
definition: "Relatively narrow, deep depression with steep sides, the bottom of which generally has a continuous slope." [ADL:FTT]

label: river valley
definition: "A valley that contains, and has been formed by, a river." [MA:ma]

label: hanging valley
definition: "A tributary valley with the floor at a higher relief than the main channel into which it flows. They are most commonly associated with U-shaped valleys when a tributary glacier flows into a glacier of larger volume." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valley#Hanging_valleys]

label: glacial valley
definition: "A valley that contains, or contained, a glacier and was formed by glacial activity. Typically U-shaped in cross-section." [MA:ma]

label: submarine canyon
definition: "A steep-sided valley on the sea floor of the continental slope. Many submarine canyons are found as extensions to large rivers; however there are many that have no such association. Canyons cutting the continental slopes have been found at depths greater than 2 km below sea level. Many submarine canyons continue as submarine channels across continental rise areas and may extend for hundreds of kilometers." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine_canyon]

label: rift valley
definition: "A valley created by the formation of a rift, i.e. place where a planet's lithosphere is being pulled apart by tectonic forces." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_valley]

label: dune slack
definition: "A valley or trough between two dunes." [MA:ma]

label: ria
definition: "A submergent coastal landform that forms where sea levels rise relative to the land either as a result of eustatic sea level change; where the global sea levels rise or isostatic sea level change; where the land sinks. When this happens valleys which were previously at sea level become submerged." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ria]

label: tunnel valley
definition: "A deep but narrow valley with a 'U' shaped cross-section and frequently a 'U' shaped plan which is usually found filled with glacial till. It is formed when the edge of an ice mass advances up a slope. Its length may be appropriately measured in centimetres or kilometres, depending on the circumstances of formation." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_valley]

label: Nye channel
definition: "A small tunnel valley." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_valley]

label: dell
definition: "A small wooded valley, either U- or V-shaped." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell_%28landform%29]

label: calanque
definition: "A deep valley with steep sides, typically of limestone, in part submerged by the sea." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calanque]

label: dry stream valley
definition: "A dry valley which was formed as a result of erosion due to stream formation and flow." []

label: dry river valley
definition: "A dry stream valley which was formed as a result of erosion due to river formation and flow." []

label: ravine
definition: "A ravine is a small, narrow, steep-sided valley that is larger than a gully and smaller than a canyon and that is usually worn by running water." [http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/ravine]

label: somma volcano
definition: "A volcanic caldera that has been partially filled by a new central cone." [wiki:http\\\://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somma]

label: tuya
definition: "A distinctive, flat-topped, steep-sided volcano formed when lava erupts through a thick glacier or ice sheet." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuya]

label: complex volcano
definition: "A volcano with more than one feature. They form because changes of their eruptive characteristics or the location of multiple vents in an area. Stratovolcanoes may form complex volcanoes, because they may overlap another from explosive eruptions, lava flows, pyroclastic flows and by repeated eruptions, to make multiple summits and vents. Stratovolcanoes could also form a large caldera that gets filled in by multiple small cinder cones, lava domes and craters may also develop on the caldera's rim." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_volcano]

label: pyroclastic shield volcano
definition: "A shield volcano that is formed mostly of pyroclastic and highly explosive eruptions rather than relatively fluid basaltic lava issuing from vents or fissures on the surface of the volcano. They typically display low-angle flank slopes and have little or no central collapse, although a shallow sag in the shield is commonly observed. Lava is commonly extruded after the cessation of explosive activity commonly superposes the vent region." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyroclastic_shield]

label: mud volcano
definition: "A volcano created by geologically excreted liquids and gases, although there are several different processes which may cause such activity. Temperatures are much cooler than igneous processes." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mud_volcano]

label: shield volcano
definition: "A large volcano with shallowly-sloping sides." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shield_volcano]

label: stratovolcano
definition: "A tall, conical volcano composed of many layers of hardened lava, tephra, and volcanic ash. These volcanoes are characterized by a steep profile and periodic, explosive eruptions. The lava that flows from them is viscous, and cools and hardens before spreading very far. The source magma of this rock is classified as acidic, or high in silica to intermediate (rhyolite, dacite, or andesite)." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratovolcano]

label: subglacial volcano
definition: "A volcano produced by subglacial eruptions or eruptions beneath the surface of a lake melted into a glacier or ice mass by the rising lava." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subglacial_volcano]

label: volcanic fissure
definition: "A linear volcanic vent through which lava erupts, usually without any explosive activity. The vent is usually a few meters wide and may be many kilometers long. Fissure vents can cause large flood basalts and hannels. The volcano can usually be seen as a crack in the ground or on the ocean floor. Narrow fissures can be filled in with lava that hardens." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fissure_vent]

label: andesitic volcano
definition: "A volcano which has been formed as a result of the eruption of andesitic lava." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andesite, https://www.pmfias.com/volcanism-andesitic-basaltic-lava-distribution-of-volcanoes/]

label: dacitic volcano
definition: "A volcano which has been formed as a result of the eruption of dacitic lava." []

label: alpine glacier
definition: "A glacier contained in the site of a mountain valley." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpine_glacier, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacier#Types, https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2004/1216/text.html]

label: ice sheet
definition: "A glacier which covers an area of greater than 50,000 square kilometers." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_sheet]

label: tidewater glacier
definition: "A glacier which terminates in a lake or the sea, with terminus either floating or grounded" [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4808-4736]

label: plateau glacier
definition: "A glacier on a plateau or high area, smaller than an ice sheet." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers]

label: valley glacier
definition: "A glacier which 1) flows for all or most of its length within the walls of a valley, in consequence having a distinct tongue and a well-defined outline and 2) descends from either high mountains, from an ice cap on a plateau, or from an ice sheet." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4808-4736]

label: outlet glacier
definition: "A glacier fed by an ice sheet." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers]

label: ice piedmont
definition: "A glacier covering a coastal strip of low-lying land backed by mountains, and sloping gently seaward over a distance up to 30km or more to terminate in ice cliffs or to merge with an ice shelf." [http://www.antarctica.ac.uk/apc/genericterms.html]

label: volcanic crater glacier
definition: "A glacier which is contained in the site bounded by a volcanic crater." []

label: branched valley glacier
definition: "A valley glacier which has one or more tributary glaciers as parts." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4808-4736]

label: simple valley glacier
definition: "A valley glacier which does not have any tributary glaciers flowing into it." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidewater_glacier#Types_of_glaciers, https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4808-4736]

label: tributary glacier
definition: "A glacier which flows into a larger glacier." [https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4808-4736]

label: cirque glacier
definition: "A small glacier contained within a cirque basin." [https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/2004/1216/text.html]

label: polar stratospheric cloud
definition: "Polar stratospheric clouds are clouds which form in the winter polar stratosphere at altitudes of 15,000–25,000 metres and which support chemical reactions that produce active chlorine and remove gaseous nitric acid, catalysing ozone destruction." [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_stratospheric_cloud]

label: cirrus homogenitus cloud
definition: "A cloud which is cirriform and is formed by condensation events centred on an aircraft's contrail." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud] {comment="https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/homogenitus.html", comment="https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html"}

label: cirrus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into detached fibrous filaments, 2) is almost exclusively composed of ice crystals, 3) is located in the high level of the atmosphere (high étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-cirrus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: homomutatus cloud
definition: "An aeroform which is formed as a result of strong upper winds spreading a cirrus homogenitus cloud in the atmosphere and, in turn, causing internal tranformations which result in the cloud taking on the appearnce of natural cirri-form clouds." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/homomutatus.html]

label: cirrocumulus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into structural elements resembling grains or ripples, 2) is almost exclusively composed of ice crystals, 3) is located in the high level of the atmosphere (high étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-cirrocumulus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrostratus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) occurs in the form of a smooth or fibrous veil, 2) is composed of few small ice crystals, 3) is located in the high level of the atmosphere (high étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-cirrostratus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: altocumulus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into laminae, rounded masses or rolls, 2) is exclusively composed of water droplets, 3) is located in the middle level of the atmosphere (middle étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-altocumulus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: altostratus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) occurs in the form of a striated, fibrous, or uniform sheet or layer, 2) is composed of water droplets and ice crystals, 3) is located in the middle level of the atmosphere (middle étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-altostratus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: nimbostratus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) occurs in the form of a layer, 2) is composed of water droplets (sometimes supercooled) and raindrops, or snow crystals and snowflakes, or of a mixture of these liquid and solid particles, 3) is located in the middle level of the atmosphere (middle étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: stratocumulus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into non-fibrous tessellations, rounded masses, or rolls, 2) is primarily composed of water droplets, and may contain raindrops or, more rarely, snow pellets, snow crystals and snowflakes, 3) is located in the low level of the atmosphere (low étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-stratocumulus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: stratus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) occurs in the form of a layer with a fairly uniform base or, less frequently, ragged patches, 2) is composed of small water droplets, 3) is located in the low level of the atmosphere (low étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-stratus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cumulus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into rising mounds, domes, or towers with a bulging upper part resembling a cauliflower and a near horizontal or ragged base, 2) is mainly composed of water droplets, 3) is located in the low level of the atmosphere (low étage)." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-cumulus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: homogenitus cloud
definition: "A cloud which is formed by condensation events triggered by some anthropogenic processes or the outputs thereof, such as aircraft contrails or emissions from chimneys." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/homogenitus.html, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: silvagenitus cloud
definition: "A cloud which develop locally over forests as a result of increased humidity due to evaporation and evapotranspiration from the tree canopy." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/silvagenitus.html, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrus fibratus cloud
definition: "A cirrus cloud which occurs as a detached unit or a thin veil and consists of nearly straight or irregularly curved filaments that do not terminate in hooks or tufts." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-fibratus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cumulonimbus cloud
definition: "A cloud which 1) has been shaped into dense, mountain-like forms or one or more tower-like forms with a flattened upper portion, which often spreads out in the shape of an anvil or plume, 2) is composed of water droplets and, especially in its upper portion, ice crystals, 3) is located in the low level of the atmosphere (low étage), but can extend into the middle and high level of the atmosphere." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera-cumulonimbus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrus uncinus cloud
definition: "A cirrus cloud which does not have grey parts and which is often shaped like a comma, terminating at its highest point in a hook, or in a tuft, the upper part of which is not in the form of a rounded protuberance." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-uncinus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrus spissatus cloud
definition: "A cirrus cloud which 1) is structurally organised in patches, 2) is sufficiently dense to appear greyish when viewed towards the local star and 3) may veil, the local star, obscure its outline, or even hide it entirely." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-spissatus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrostratus fibratus cloud
definition: "A cirrostratus cloud which occurs as a detached unit or a thin veil and consists of nearly straight or irregularly curved filaments that do not terminate in hooks or tufts." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-fibratus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: stratocumulus castellanus cloud
definition: "A stratocumulus cloud which 1) has linearly arranged cumuliform protuberances which resemble crenellated turrets or towers, some of which are taller than they are wide in some portion of their upper parts, 2) possess a lower region or base which connects these protuberances." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-castellanus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrus castellanus cloud
definition: "A cirrus cloud which 1) has linearly arranged cumuliform protuberances which resemble crenellated turrets or towers, some of which are taller than they are wide in some portion of their upper parts, 2) possess a lower region or base which connects these protuberances." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-castellanus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: cirrocumulus castellanus cloud
definition: "A cirrocumulus cloud which 1) has linearly arranged cumuliform protuberances which resemble crenellated turrets or towers, some of which are taller than they are wide in some portion of their upper parts, 2) possess a lower region or base which connects these protuberances." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-castellanus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: altocumulus castellanus cloud
definition: "An altocumulus cloud which 1) has linearly arranged cumuliform protuberances which resemble crenellated turrets or towers, some of which are taller than they are wide in some portion of their upper parts, 2) possess a lower region or base which connects these protuberances." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-genera.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/clouds-species-castellanus.html, https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/docs/Excerpt%20from%20wmo_49-1_final_2017.pdf, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]

label: water-based cloud
definition: "A cloud which is primarily composed of water-based aerosols." [https://cloudatlas.wmo.int/introduction-and-principles-of-cloud-classification.html, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud]
